title: FRP Grating Glossary: 49 Technical Terms Every Engineer Should Know
author: Engineering Team
excerpt: A complete FRP grating glossary covering 49 essential technical terms: materials, manufacturing, mechanical properties, standards, resins, and application terminology used by specifiers, buyers, and engineers worldwide.
content:
Why This Glossary Matters

FRP (Fiber Reinforced Polymer) grating has its own technical vocabulary. Specifying the wrong term can lead to costly ordering mistakes, installation errors, and project delays. This glossary defines the 49 most commonly used terms in the fiberglass grating industry, organized by category for quick reference.

1. Material & Fiber Terms

E-glass (Electrical Glass): The most common glass fiber type, offering good electrical insulation and mechanical properties. Used in general-purpose FRP products.

C-glass (Chemical Glass): Glass fiber with superior corrosion resistance to acidic environments, used in chemical processing applications.

S-glass (High-Strength Glass): Higher tensile strength and modulus than E-glass, used in demanding structural applications.

Fiberglass Fabric / Woven Roving: A textile made from woven glass fibers, used as reinforcement in FRP lamination and composite fabrication.

Fiberglass Mesh: Open-weave glass fiber fabric used for reinforcement in construction, wall insulation, and composite repairs.

Fiberglass Tape: Narrow strips of woven glass fiber used for edge reinforcement, sealing, and joint finishing.

Chopped Strand Mat (CSM): Randomly oriented glass fibers held together by binder, used for hand lay-up and surface finishing.

Continuous Roving: Long, untwisted glass fiber strands wound on spools, used in pultrusion and filament winding.

2. Resin Systems

Orthophthalic Polyester: General-purpose resin with good mechanical properties and moderate corrosion resistance. The most cost-effective resin for standard applications.

Isophthalic Polyester: Improved corrosion resistance over ortho resin, suitable for moderately aggressive chemical environments.

Vinyl Ester: High-performance resin with excellent corrosion resistance to acids, alkalies, and solvents. Preferred for chemical plants and offshore applications.

Resin Content: The percentage of resin in an FRP part, typically 25-40% by weight. Higher resin content improves corrosion resistance but reduces strength.

Gel Coat: A thin outer layer of unreinforced resin that provides surface protection and UV resistance.

3. Manufacturing Processes

Pultrusion: A continuous process where reinforced fibers are pulled through a resin bath and heated die to produce constant-cross-section profiles.

Molded Grating Process: Fiberglass strands are laid in a grid pattern and saturated with resin in a heated mold, creating a one-piece bidirectional grid.

Hand Lay-up: Manual process where glass fabric and resin are applied layer by layer in an open mold.

Filament Winding: Continuous fibers are wound over a rotating mandrel under tension to produce hollow cylindrical shapes.

Curing: The chemical reaction that transforms liquid resin into a solid polymer matrix, typically accelerated by heat.

Post-curing: Additional heat treatment after initial cure to maximize resin cross-linking and mechanical properties.

4. Mechanical & Physical Properties

Tensile Strength: The maximum stress a material can withstand while being stretched, measured in MPa or psi.

Bending Strength (Flexural Strength): The stress at failure when a beam is loaded transversely.

Compressive Strength: The capacity of a material to withstand loads that reduce its size.

Elastic Modulus (Young's Modulus): A measure of stiffness, defined as stress divided by strain in the elastic region.

Deflection: The degree to which a structural element bends under load. Grating deflection limits are typically L/200 or L/150.

Barcol Hardness: A measure of surface hardness for reinforced plastics, typically 40-60 for FRP grating.

Specific Gravity: The ratio of density to water. FRP grating weighs about 1/4 of steel grating.

Impact Strength: The ability to absorb shock energy without fracture, measured in ft-lb/in or J.

Fatigue Resistance: The ability to withstand repeated loading cycles without failure.

5. Grating-Specific Terms

Mesh Size: The clear opening between bearing bars, typically 38×38mm, 40×40mm, or 50×50mm.

Bearing Bar: The primary load-carrying bar in pultruded grating, running in one direction.

Cross Bar: The transverse bar that connects bearing bars and maintains grid spacing.

Bar Thickness / Depth: The dimension of the bearing bar, commonly 25, 38, 50, or 75mm.

Span: The distance between supporting points. Load capacity is directly related to span length.

Safety Factor: The ratio of ultimate load to design load, typically 3:1 or 4:1 for industrial grating.

Anti-slip Surface: A gritted or serrated top surface that provides traction in wet or oily conditions.

Grating Clips / Fasteners: Metal or FRP clamps used to secure grating panels to support structures.

6. Standards & Certifications

ASTM E-84: Standard test method for surface burning characteristics of building materials. FRP grating typically achieves Class B.

ASTM D3299: Standard specification for glass-fiber-reinforced thermosetting resin wall (ortho polyester).

ASTM D4162: Standard specification for glass-fiber-reinforced thermosetting resin wall (vinyl ester).

ISO 9001: International quality management system certification ensuring consistent manufacturing quality.

ABS (American Bureau of Shipping): Certification for products used in marine and offshore applications.

Intertek / SGS / TÜV: Third-party testing and certification bodies verifying product performance claims.

7. Application & Installation Terms

Walkway / Pedestrian Grating: Grating designed for foot traffic, typically 25-38mm thick.

Wheel Load Rating: The maximum wheel load the grating can support, critical for forklift or trolley traffic.

Curb / Toe Board: A vertical barrier at walkway edges to prevent objects from falling.

Handrail System: A FRP tubular safety railing system, typically paired with grating walkways.

Stair Tread: A grated panel designed for use as a stair step, with anti-slip surface and nosing.

Drainage Cover: Grating used to cover drains, trenches, or pits while allowing water passage.

FRP Covers & Panels: Solid or perforated fiberglass panels used for sun shading, equipment enclosures, and screening.

OEM/ODM: Original Equipment Manufacturer / Original Design Manufacturer — custom production to buyer specifications.
